I have farmed this pattern for many years, so I will not change too much at once. On 16.1 mu with wheat-maize rotation, I will put the full 16.1 mu through wheat in the winter season and the same 16.1 mu through maize in the summer season. I have well water, so I will not be stingy on key irrigations, because once wheat misses water at jointing or maize misses water around tasseling, yield drops fast and that loss is bigger than the extra electricity and fertilizer bill. I finished middle school, so I do look at input cost and yield together. I usually start from what worked last year, then adjust a little by crop condition, fertilizer price, and what farmers around me are doing. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger because wheat here needs a steady stand and good ears, and I will split nitrogen between base and topdressing. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen solid, and not let the field go short at the big-mouth to tasseling stage. I will do rotary tillage after each harvest because it is practical for my size, fast enough for the next crop, and suits our local habit.
